title: Separate facts, interpretation, and invention
use_cases: Use when repurposing canonical source material into a new medium
Implement when developing a structured research framework to maintain factual accuracy
Configure when establishing editorial guidelines for creative writing and fan fiction
Use when documenting the distinction between original sources and critical analysis
content:
Canonical works often carry enormous cultural weight, which makes factual precision essential. Before you publish, clearly distinguish what comes from the source, what comes from your interpretation, and what is your own creative invention. This clarity protects your trustworthiness and helps search engines understand the intent of your page. It also reduces disputes with readers who may be sensitive to changes in character, timeline, or theme.

One useful trick is to build a three-column research sheet: “what the source says,” “what critics say it means,” and “what I’m doing differently.” That structure can save you from accidental misrepresentation, especially when you are repurposing the work into a new medium. For creators who have to manage tight deadlines, a disciplined research workflow is as important as any equipment choice, much like choosing the right recording setup matters for audio quality. Accuracy is not an aesthetic bonus; it is a credibility asset.
